description: Comprehensive question bank on Analytical Reasoning (Mental Ability 15.2) derived from official FDA/SDA notes. Covers Puzzles, Arrangements, Classification, Analogy, Ranking, Ordering, and Mathematical/Positional Tools.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is analytical reasoning?

options.A: Memorising facts without analysis
options.B: The systematic examination of facts, conditions, relationships, and constraints to solve a problem or identify a result that satisfies the given information

questions.explanation: Analytical reasoning is the systematic examination of facts, conditions, relationships, and constraints to solve a problem or identify a result that satisfies the information given.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between logical reasoning and analytical reasoning?

options.A: They are exactly the same with no difference
options.B: Logical reasoning tests whether conclusions follow from premises, while analytical reasoning commonly requires organising several facts or conditions—often in tables, diagrams, or ordered lists—to solve a structured problem
options.D: Logical reasoning does not require premises

questions.explanation: Logical reasoning broadly tests whether conclusions follow from premises. Analytical reasoning commonly requires organising several facts or conditions—often in tables, diagrams, or ordered lists—to solve a structured problem. The two areas overlap.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a constraint in an analytical-reasoning problem?

options.A: An optional suggestion
options.B: A condition that every valid answer must satisfy

questions.explanation: A constraint is a condition that every valid answer must satisfy, such as 'A sits immediately to the left of B' or 'C is not assigned to Monday'.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a definite condition?

options.A: A condition that rules out a possibility
options.B: A condition that directly fixes a fact or relationship
options.C: A condition that establishes a relative relationship without fixing exact positions
options.D: A condition that is always false

questions.explanation: A definite condition directly fixes a fact or relationship, such as 'Ravi is in position 3'.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a negative condition?

options.A: A condition that directly fixes a fact
options.B: A condition that rules out a possibility
options.C: A condition that establishes relative order
options.D: A condition that is always true

questions.explanation: A negative condition rules out a possibility, such as 'Maya does not sit at either end'.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a relative condition?

options.A: A condition that fixes exact positions
options.B: A condition that rules out all possibilities
options.C: A condition that establishes a relationship without fixing exact positions
options.D: A condition that is impossible to satisfy

questions.explanation: A relative condition establishes a relationship without fixing exact positions, such as 'A is older than B' or 'P is somewhere before Q'.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the best general method for solving analytical-reasoning questions?

options.A: Solve mentally without writing anything
options.B: Read all conditions, identify entities and positions, draw a table or diagram, enter fixed facts first, apply negative and relative conditions, eliminate contradictions, and verify every condition
options.C: Choose the first option that looks correct

questions.explanation: Read all conditions, identify the entities and available positions or categories, draw a suitable table or diagram, enter fixed facts first, apply negative and relative conditions, eliminate contradictions, and verify every condition before selecting an answer.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Why should a candidate avoid solving a puzzle mentally without a diagram?

options.A: Because diagrams are not allowed in exams
options.B: Because a diagram or table reduces working-memory errors, makes relationships visible, and helps track multiple conditions accurately
options.C: Because mental solving is always wrong
options.D: Because diagrams slow down the process unnecessarily

questions.explanation: A diagram or table reduces working-memory errors, makes relationships visible, and helps track multiple conditions accurately—especially when several people, days, floors, or positions are involved.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a puzzle in analytical reasoning?

options.A: A problem that requires only calculation
options.B: A problem in which several facts and conditions must be combined to determine an arrangement, assignment, sequence, or relationship
options.D: A problem that tests vocabulary only

questions.explanation: A puzzle is a problem in which several facts and conditions must be combined to determine an arrangement, assignment, sequence, or relationship.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common type of reasoning puzzle?

options.A: Seating puzzles

questions.explanation: Common types include seating puzzles, floor or building puzzles, day-and-time scheduling, person-profession-city matching, box or shelf arrangements, age puzzles, comparison puzzles, and distribution or assignment puzzles. Poetry composition is not a listed type.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a linear arrangement puzzle?

options.A: A puzzle that places people around a circle
options.B: A puzzle that places people or objects in a straight line, usually facing the same or opposite direction, and asks about positions and neighbours
options.C: A puzzle that assigns people to floors
options.D: A puzzle that matches people with professions

questions.explanation: A linear arrangement puzzle places people or objects in a straight line, usually facing the same or opposite direction, and asks questions about positions and neighbours.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a circular arrangement puzzle?

options.A: A puzzle that places people in a straight row
options.B: A puzzle that places people or objects around a circle where conditions may specify who sits next to, opposite, or between whom
options.C: A puzzle that assigns events to days

questions.explanation: A circular arrangement puzzle places people or objects around a circle. Conditions may specify who sits next to, opposite, or between whom.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a floor-based puzzle?

options.A: A puzzle that assigns people to days of the week
options.B: A puzzle that assigns people or objects to different floors of a building using clues such as above, below, immediately above, or not on the top floor
options.C: A puzzle that places people around a circle
options.D: A puzzle that groups items by shared property

questions.explanation: A floor-based puzzle assigns people or objects to different floors of a building using clues such as above, below, immediately above, or not on the top floor.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a scheduling puzzle?

options.A: A puzzle that assigns events, people, or tasks to days, dates, or time slots while satisfying conditions about order, gaps, and restrictions
options.B: A puzzle that places people in a straight line
options.C: A puzzle that identifies the odd item out
options.D: A puzzle that tests synonym relationships

questions.explanation: A scheduling puzzle assigns events, people, or tasks to days, dates, or time slots while satisfying conditions about order, gaps, and restrictions.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a matching or distribution puzzle?

options.A: A puzzle that connects items from two or more categories—for example, each person with one city, one subject, or one occupation—without violating the given conditions
options.B: A puzzle that places people around a circle
options.C: A puzzle that asks for the shortest person
options.D: A puzzle that tests letter patterns only

questions.explanation: A matching puzzle connects items from two or more categories—for example, each person with one city, one subject, or one occupation—without violating the given conditions.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a comparison puzzle?

options.A: A puzzle that establishes relative relationships such as taller/shorter, older/younger, heavier/lighter, or higher/lower, and asks for a ranking or relationship
options.B: A puzzle that assigns people to floors
options.C: A puzzle that identifies the odd word out
options.D: A puzzle that tests alphabet shifts

questions.explanation: A comparison puzzle establishes relative relationships such as taller/shorter, older/younger, heavier/lighter, or higher/lower, and asks for a ranking or relationship.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How should a puzzle with several categories be represented?

options.A: By writing a paragraph of text
options.B: By using a grid or table with one category as rows and another as columns, marking confirmed matches, exclusions, and unresolved possibilities distinctly
options.C: By memorising all clues without writing
options.D: By ignoring categories that seem unimportant

questions.explanation: Use a grid or table with one category as rows and another as columns. Mark confirmed matches, exclusions, and unresolved possibilities distinctly.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'exactly one' mean in a puzzle?

options.A: Zero or one

questions.explanation: Exactly one means one and only one. It excludes both zero and two or more possibilities.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'at least one' mean?

options.A: Exactly one

questions.explanation: At least one means one or more; it does not mean exactly one.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'at most one' mean?

options.A: One or more

questions.explanation: At most one means zero or one; two or more are not permitted.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'one of the following' mean in aptitude questions?

options.A: It always means exactly two
options.B: It may mean exactly one in many aptitude questions, but the candidate must follow the wording and any explicit conditions rather than assume an unstated interpretation
options.C: It means none of the options
options.D: It means all options are correct

questions.explanation: The phrase may mean exactly one in many aptitude questions, but the candidate must follow the wording and any explicit conditions rather than assume an unstated interpretation.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'either A or B, but not both' mean?

options.A: Both A and B are true
options.B: Both A and B are false
options.C: Exactly one of A and B is true
options.D: At least one of A and B is true, possibly both

questions.explanation: It is an exclusive choice: exactly one of A and B is true.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'neither A nor B' mean?

options.A: Both A and B are true
options.B: Both A and B are false
options.C: Exactly one of A and B is true

questions.explanation: Both A and B are false.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'both A and B' mean?

options.A: A and B are simultaneously true

questions.explanation: A and B are simultaneously true.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How should a candidate handle a puzzle with insufficient information?

options.A: Invent a unique answer
options.B: Do not invent a unique answer; identify what is definitely established, retain multiple valid possibilities where necessary, and choose only an option supported by all the clues

questions.explanation: Do not invent a unique answer. Identify what is definitely established, retain multiple valid possibilities where necessary, and choose only an option that is supported by all the clues.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a case-based puzzle?

options.A: A puzzle solved by guessing
options.B: A puzzle solved by splitting the problem into possible cases, applying the conditions to each case, and eliminating any case that creates a contradiction
options.D: A puzzle that only uses numbers

questions.explanation: A case-based puzzle is solved by splitting the problem into possible cases, applying the conditions to each case, and eliminating any case that creates a contradiction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the importance of checking all clues at the end?

options.A: It is unnecessary if the answer looks correct
options.B: A proposed arrangement may satisfy most clues but violate one; a final condition-by-condition check confirms that the solution is valid
options.C: It wastes time and should be avoided

questions.explanation: A proposed arrangement may satisfy most clues but violate one. A final condition-by-condition check confirms that the solution is valid.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is arrangement in analytical reasoning?

options.A: The placement of people or objects in positions according to given conditions such as direction, adjacency, distance, order, or relative position
options.B: The process of grouping items by shared property
options.C: The relationship between two pairs of words
options.D: The calculation of rank from both ends

questions.explanation: Arrangement is the placement of people or objects in positions according to given conditions such as direction, adjacency, distance, order, or relative position.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a linear seating arrangement?

options.A: An arrangement of people around a circle
options.B: An arrangement of people in a straight row where questions commonly ask about left, right, immediate neighbours, ends, and positions from either side
options.C: An arrangement of people on different floors
options.D: An arrangement of events on different days

questions.explanation: It is an arrangement of people in a straight row. Questions commonly ask about left, right, immediate neighbours, ends, and positions from either side.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is left and right interpreted when everyone faces north in a row?

options.A: Left and right are reversed relative to a south-facing diagram
options.B: A person's left is the left side from that person's perspective; when all face north, their left generally corresponds to the west side of the page and their right to the east side
options.C: Left and right are determined by the examiner's viewpoint only
options.D: Left and right have no meaning in a row

questions.explanation: A person's left is the left side from that person's perspective. When all face north, their left generally corresponds to the west side of the page and their right to the east side.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is left and right interpreted when everyone faces south in a row?

options.A: Left and right are the same as when facing north
options.B: When all face south, the person's left and right are reversed relative to a north-facing diagram; always mark the facing direction before placing people
options.C: Left and right cannot be determined
options.D: Only right is meaningful when facing south

questions.explanation: When all face south, the person's left and right are reversed relative to a north-facing diagram. Always mark the facing direction before placing people.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How should left and right be handled when people face opposite directions?

options.A: Interpret left and right from the examiner's viewpoint
options.B: Interpret left and right from each person's own facing direction, not from the examiner's viewpoint; mark each person's direction separately
options.D: Assume everyone faces the same direction

questions.explanation: Interpret left and right from each person's own facing direction, not from the examiner's viewpoint. Mark each person's direction separately.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'A sits immediately to the left of B' mean?

options.A: A occupies the position directly adjacent to B on B's left, according to B's facing direction
options.B: A is somewhere to the left of B, not necessarily adjacent
options.C: A sits between B and C

questions.explanation: A occupies the position directly adjacent to B on B's left, according to B's facing direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'A sits somewhere to the left of B' mean?

options.A: A is immediately adjacent to B
options.B: A is located at any position on B's left side; A need not be immediately adjacent to B

questions.explanation: A is located at any position on B's left side; A need not be immediately adjacent to B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'A sits between B and C' mean?

options.A: A is positioned between B and C in the stated arrangement; unless the question says 'immediately', other people may be present between them
options.B: A is immediately adjacent to both B and C
options.D: A is at one end of the row

questions.explanation: A is positioned between B and C in the stated arrangement. Unless the question says 'immediately between', other people may be present between them.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'A is second to the right of B' mean?

options.A: A is immediately to the right of B
options.B: Starting from B and moving two positions to the right according to B's facing direction leads to A
options.C: A is two positions to the left of B

questions.explanation: Starting from B and moving two positions to the right according to B's facing direction leads to A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'A is adjacent to B' mean?

options.A: A and B occupy neighbouring positions with no person or object between them
options.B: A and B are at opposite ends
options.C: A and B are separated by exactly two people
options.D: A is somewhere to the left of B

questions.explanation: A and B occupy neighbouring positions with no person or object between them.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'A is opposite B' mean in a circular arrangement?

options.A: A and B are adjacent to each other
options.B: A and B occupy positions directly across the circle from one another; this is possible only when the number and spacing of seats allow a directly opposite position
options.C: A sits between B and C
options.D: A is immediately to the left of B

questions.explanation: A and B occupy positions directly across the circle from one another. This is possible only when the number and spacing of seats allow a directly opposite position.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'A is an immediate neighbour of B' mean?

options.A: A occupies one of the positions directly next to B
options.B: A is somewhere to the left of B
options.D: A is two positions away from B

questions.explanation: A occupies one of the positions directly next to B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How are positions counted in a row?

options.A: Positions are counted from the specified end or direction; the first position is the end position, and the count increases one place at a time
options.B: Positions are counted from the middle outward
options.D: Positions are counted only from the left

questions.explanation: Positions are counted from the specified end or direction. The first position is the end position, and the count increases one place at a time.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How should circular seating puzzles be drawn?

options.A: Draw a square with people at corners
options.B: Draw a circle with equally spaced positions, mark one person's position as a reference to remove rotational duplication, and then apply clockwise, anticlockwise, neighbour, and opposite clues
options.D: Draw a vertical list of floors

questions.explanation: Draw a circle with equally spaced positions, mark one person's position as a reference to remove rotational duplication, and then apply clockwise, anticlockwise, neighbour, and opposite clues.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Does rotating a circular arrangement create a different arrangement?

options.A: Yes, every rotation is a new arrangement
options.B: No, a rotation preserves the relative seating order; unless seats are numbered or fixed landmarks are given, one person can be fixed at a reference position to simplify the diagram
options.C: Only clockwise rotation creates a new arrangement

questions.explanation: A rotation preserves the relative seating order. Unless seats are numbered or fixed landmarks are given, one person can be fixed at a reference position to simplify the diagram.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Does reflecting a circular arrangement always create the same arrangement?

options.A: Yes, reflection always gives the same arrangement
options.B: No, reflection reverses clockwise and anticlockwise order; it may produce a distinct arrangement unless the puzzle's conditions make the mirror image equivalent
options.C: Reflection is not possible in circular arrangements
options.D: Reflection only applies to linear arrangements

questions.explanation: Reflection reverses clockwise and anticlockwise order. It may produce a distinct arrangement unless the puzzle's conditions make the mirror image equivalent.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'clockwise' mean in a circular arrangement?

options.A: In the direction opposite to the hands of a conventional clock
options.B: In the same direction as the hands of a conventional clock

questions.explanation: Clockwise means in the same direction as the hands of a conventional clock.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'anticlockwise' mean?

options.A: In the same direction as the hands of a conventional clock
options.B: In the direction opposite to the hands of a conventional clock

questions.explanation: Anticlockwise means in the direction opposite to the hands of a conventional clock.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a double-row seating arrangement?

options.A: Two parallel rows, often with people in one row facing people in the other; directions must be interpreted separately for each row
options.B: A single row with people facing north only
options.C: A circular arrangement with two people

questions.explanation: It involves two parallel rows, often with people in one row facing people in the other. Directions must be interpreted separately for each row.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a rectangular or square arrangement?

options.A: People or objects are placed in a single straight line
options.B: People or objects are placed around the sides or corners of a rectangle or square; clues may refer to corners, sides, opposite positions, and adjacent positions
options.C: People are placed on different floors
options.D: People are placed around a circle only

questions.explanation: People or objects are placed around the sides or corners of a rectangle or square. Clues may refer to corners, sides, opposite positions, and adjacent positions.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a floor arrangement?

options.A: It assigns people or objects to floors in a building; establish whether the lowest floor is numbered 1 or whether numbering is otherwise specified
options.B: It assigns people to seats around a table
options.D: It connects a tool to its user

questions.explanation: It assigns people or objects to floors in a building. Establish whether the lowest floor is numbered 1 or whether numbering is otherwise specified.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'immediately above' mean in a floor puzzle?

options.A: On the floor directly one level higher, with no floor between the two
options.B: Two floors above with one floor between

questions.explanation: It means on the floor directly one level higher, with no floor between the two.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'two floors above' mean?

options.A: On the floor directly one level higher
options.B: There is a difference of two floor levels; one floor lies between the two people or objects

questions.explanation: It means there is a difference of two floor levels; one floor lies between the two people or objects.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the most reliable way to solve a floor puzzle?

options.A: Draw a horizontal row of people
options.B: Draw a vertical list of floors, enter fixed floors first, translate above/below clues into relative positions, and check top-floor and bottom-floor restrictions
options.C: Guess the answer from the options

questions.explanation: Draw a vertical list of floors, enter fixed floors first, translate above/below clues into relative positions, and check top-floor and bottom-floor restrictions.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is classification in analytical reasoning?

options.A: The process of grouping items according to a shared property or identifying the item that does not belong to a given group
options.B: The placement of people in rows
options.C: The relationship between two pairs of words
options.D: The calculation of total people from ranks

questions.explanation: Classification is the process of grouping items according to a shared property or identifying the item that does not belong to a given group.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the odd-one-out question?

options.A: It presents several words, numbers, letters, shapes, or objects and asks which one differs from the others according to a consistent rule
options.B: It asks to arrange people in a circle
options.C: It asks for the rank from the bottom
options.D: It asks to complete an analogy

questions.explanation: It presents several words, numbers, letters, shapes, or objects and asks which one differs from the others according to a consistent rule.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common base of classification?

options.A: Meaning

questions.explanation: Common bases include meaning, category, use, function, physical property, shape, size, number pattern, letter pattern, spelling, pronunciation, alphabetical order, and relationship. Clockwise direction is not a classification base.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How are words classified in odd-one-out questions?

options.A: Only by their first letter
options.B: Words may be grouped by category, meaning, part of speech, function, origin, spelling pattern, number of letters, or relationship; identify the most consistent common feature

questions.explanation: Words may be grouped by category, meaning, part of speech, function, origin, spelling pattern, number of letters, or relationship. Identify the most consistent common feature.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How are numbers classified?

options.A: Only by their size
options.B: Numbers may be grouped by parity, prime/composite status, factors, multiples, squares, cubes, digit sum, divisibility, place value, or a mathematical sequence
options.D: Only by whether they are positive

questions.explanation: Numbers may be grouped by parity, prime/composite status, factors, multiples, squares, cubes, digit sum, divisibility, place value, or a mathematical sequence.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is classification by parity?

options.A: It groups integers as even or odd; an even integer is divisible by 2, and an odd integer is not divisible by 2
options.B: It groups numbers as prime or composite
options.C: It groups numbers by their digit sum
options.D: It groups numbers as positive or negative

questions.explanation: It groups integers as even or odd. An even integer is divisible by 2; an odd integer is not divisible by 2.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a prime number?

options.A: A natural number greater than 1 with exactly two positive divisors: 1 and itself
options.B: A natural number greater than 1 with more than two positive divisors

questions.explanation: A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 with exactly two positive divisors: 1 and itself. The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a composite number?

options.A: A natural number greater than 1 that has more than two positive divisors
options.B: A natural number with exactly two divisors

questions.explanation: A composite number is a natural number greater than 1 that has more than two positive divisors.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How are letters classified in reasoning questions?

options.A: Only by their alphabetical position
options.B: Letters may be classified by alphabetical position, vowels and consonants, forward or backward sequence, symmetry, number of strokes, or repeated-letter patterns
options.C: Only by whether they are capital or small

questions.explanation: Letters may be classified by alphabetical position, vowels and consonants, forward or backward sequence, symmetry, number of strokes, or repeated-letter patterns.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is alphabetical position?

options.A: The ordinal place of a letter in the English alphabet: A = 1, B = 2, ..., Z = 26
options.B: The number of strokes in a letter
options.C: Whether a letter is a vowel or consonant

questions.explanation: It is the ordinal place of a letter in the English alphabet: A = 1, B = 2, ..., Z = 26.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How can shapes be classified?

options.A: Only by colour
options.B: Shapes may be grouped by number of sides, angles, symmetry, orientation, dimensions, shading, or internal patterns
options.D: Only by whether they are drawn with straight lines

questions.explanation: Shapes may be grouped by number of sides, angles, symmetry, orientation, dimensions, shading, or internal patterns.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the best method for an odd-one-out question?

options.A: Pick the option that looks most different
options.B: Test plausible properties across all options, find a rule that groups the largest consistent set, and avoid choosing a feature that applies to only two options arbitrarily

questions.explanation: Test plausible properties across all options, find a rule that groups the largest consistent set, and avoid choosing a feature that applies to only two options arbitrarily.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Can an odd-one-out question have more than one possible rule?

options.A: No, there is always exactly one rule
options.B: Yes; if the question is poorly designed, multiple rules may be possible, but in an examination, prefer the simplest rule that consistently explains the largest number of options
options.C: Yes, and any rule is equally acceptable
options.D: No, odd-one-out questions never have ambiguity

questions.explanation: Yes. If the question is poorly designed, multiple rules may be possible. In an examination, prefer the simplest rule that consistently explains the largest number of options.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is analogy in analytical reasoning?

options.A: It tests whether a candidate can identify a relationship between one pair of items and apply the same relationship to another item or pair
options.B: It tests the ability to group items by shared property
options.C: It tests the calculation of ranks

questions.explanation: Analogy tests whether a candidate can identify a relationship between one pair of items and apply the same relationship to another item or pair.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a verbal analogy?

options.A: A verbal analogy uses numbers and arithmetic relationships
options.B: A verbal analogy uses words and tests relationships such as synonymy, antonymy, function, part-whole, category, cause-effect, worker-tool, or object-user
options.C: A verbal analogy uses letter positions only
options.D: A verbal analogy uses shapes only

questions.explanation: A verbal analogy uses words and tests relationships such as synonymy, antonymy, function, part-whole, category, cause-effect, worker-tool, or object-user.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a numerical analogy?

options.A: A numerical analogy uses words and tests synonyms
options.B: A numerical analogy uses numbers and asks the candidate to apply the same arithmetic or mathematical relationship from one pair to another
options.C: A numerical analogy uses letters only
options.D: A numerical analogy uses shapes only

questions.explanation: A numerical analogy uses numbers and asks the candidate to apply the same arithmetic or mathematical relationship from one pair to another.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is an alphabet analogy?

options.A: An alphabet analogy uses letter positions, forward or backward shifts, reversals, or patterns to relate one group of letters to another
options.B: An alphabet analogy uses numbers only
options.C: An alphabet analogy uses shapes only
options.D: An alphabet analogy uses words with opposite meanings only

questions.explanation: An alphabet analogy uses letter positions, forward or backward shifts, reversals, or patterns to relate one group of letters to another.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a relationship analogy?

options.A: It connects items through a meaningful relationship, such as doctor:hospital :: teacher:school, where each person is associated with a typical workplace
options.B: It connects words with similar meanings
options.C: It connects a part to a whole
options.D: It connects a cause to an effect

questions.explanation: It connects items through a meaningful relationship, such as doctor:hospital :: teacher:school, where each person is associated with a typical workplace.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a synonym analogy?

options.A: It relates words with similar meanings, such as rapid:fast
options.B: It relates words with opposite meanings
options.C: It relates a part to a whole
options.D: It relates a tool to its user

questions.explanation: It relates words with similar meanings, such as rapid:fast.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is an antonym analogy?

options.A: It relates words with similar meanings
options.B: It relates words with opposite meanings, such as ancient:modern
options.C: It relates a component to a larger entity
options.D: It relates an object to its function

questions.explanation: It relates words with opposite meanings, such as ancient:modern.
